A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, and Appendices A–E. Relocated theorems and experiments can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on XOR clusters, split MNIST, and Gaussian-mixture tasks with transformers in Section 3 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds a four-task split FashionMNIST experiment in Figure 6.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the neural-network formulation, sequential gradient updates, and previous-task L2 regularization objective are retained. The added experiment uses activation and loss choices already studied in v1.

E1.justification: v2 adds split FashionMNIST with four binary classification tasks in Figure 6, extending the represented data beyond the retained XOR, MNIST, and Gaussian-mixture tasks. MNIST's move from the appendix is not new coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically compares against competing continual-learning algorithms. The experiments continue to compare parameter configurations; newly cited methods are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The added FashionMNIST experiment uses four tasks, 200 first-task samples, 2,000 iterations per task, width 2,000, learning rate 0.05, and inputs normalized to have norm at most one. Matched earlier experiments retain their reported settings.

E4.justification: Figure 6 adds a FashionMNIST sensitivity study that fixes the first-task sample size and varies later-task sample sizes to examine forgetting. Existing analyses of width, training horizon, task count, activations, and transformer size are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging MNIST experiments over 15 runs and transformer experiments over 10 independent runs. v2 adds no corresponding run-count disclosure or new uncertainty-reporting procedure for FashionMNIST.

E6.justification: The new FashionMNIST curves in Figure 6 show substantially greater late first-task loss with 200 later-task samples than with the larger sample sizes, whose curves are closely grouped. The retained XOR, MNIST, and transformer plots preserve their results after relocation.

T1.justification: Limited mathematical edits include adding an explicit learning-rate factor eta to the first-task generalization bound in Remark B.2, compared with v1 Remark 2, and changing the stated early-stopping relation to soft-Theta(n). The principal bounds and proof arguments remain largely unchanged; v1 Theorem 4 is retained as v2 Theorem B.1.

C1.justification: The central XOR forgetting guarantees, complexity claims, and first-closed-form novelty claim are retained. v2's introduction explicitly extends the claimed applicability of its analysis approach to other distributions, anticipating similar insights for other single- or multi-index models without proving new guarantees for them.

C2.justification: Section 2.2 adds substantive discussion of which calculations specialize to XOR data and how task correlations complicate extensions. Section 2.3 explicitly limits the regularization conclusion to the studied L2/kernel setting and allows potential benefits from architectural changes or stronger feature learning.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds FashionMNIST label-selection, preprocessing, architecture, and training details. Existing experimental parameter lists and the code-access link persist, but v1's explicit construction of the experimental XOR mean vectors is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused discussions of CNN forgetting, neural tangent ensembles, representation learning, and information-flow analyses, including Li et al. (2025a), Benjamin et al. (2024), Cao et al. (2022), and Andle and Yasaei Sekeh (2022). It also revises stability citations and sharpens the existing contrast with linear-model theory.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten and expanded, and the main theoretical discussion gains substantial explanatory prose and a dedicated forgetting-decomposition subsection. The sharper generalization theorem moves to Appendix B, while the MNIST discussion moves into Section 3, substantially reorganizing the exposition.

P2.justification: The document is globally retypeset with different text and mathematical fonts, spacing, figure sizing, and placement. v1 Figure 11's MNIST panels become part of v2 Figure 6 alongside the new FashionMNIST panel, while v1 Figure 6's width analysis moves to appendix Figure 11; the remaining plots are rearranged.

improvement.justification: The FashionMNIST study adds empirical corroboration, and the expanded applicability discussion and regularization qualifications improve clarity. These limited benefits outweigh the omitted XOR mean-vector recipe. The principal guarantees remain unchanged, and Appendix B.1.1 still marks an intermediate claim as 'needs proof', so the revision does not resolve that theoretical gap.
